item.title: All Together Now: China’s Militia in 2025
item.description: China’s militia presence hits a record high.

item.title: Revitalizing U.S.-Pacific Ties Through Kava Diplomacy
item.description: With U.S. aid declining in the Pacific Islands, kava trade plays a growing role in rebuilding regional economic ties.

item.title: EST Rapid Roundup: What Comes Next for U.S. Trade Policy After the Supreme Court’s IEEPA Ruling?
item.description: CSIS Economic Security and Technology Department experts examined the economic and geopolitical implications of the Supreme Court’s tariffs decision and assessed how it could reshape the administration’s strategy and trade toolkit going forward.

item.title: What the Potomac River Sewage Spill Reveals About U.S. Water Infrastructure
item.description: On January 19, a sewer collapse outside Washington, D.C., resulted in the largest wastewater spill in U.S. history, raising concerns about the broader challenges facing U.S. water infrastructure.

item.title: State of Play: The Global Impact of the SCOTUS Decision on IEEPA Tariffs
item.description: On February 20, the U.S. Supreme Court declared President Donald Trump’s use of IEEPA to impose global tariffs against U.S. trading partners illegal. CSIS experts assess how governments and key sectors around the world are likely to interpret and react to the decision.

item.title: U.S. Military in the Middle East: Numbers Behind Trump’s Threats Against Iran
item.description: Eight months after Operation Midnight Hammer, the United States has again moved large air and naval forces to the Middle East. These can launch punitive strikes on Iran and protect U.S. allies and partners but lack the capability for ground operations, raids, or regime change.

item.title: Measles Outbreaks and Elimination in North America
item.description: The CSIS Bipartisan Alliance for Global Health Security discussed measles outbreaks and elimination in the North American context and the implications of sustained measles transmission for regional and global health security.

item.title: If Trump Strikes Iran: Mapping the Oil Disruption Scenarios
item.description: In last summer’s Twelve-Day War, energy supplies were largely spared. But in a potential new round of fighting between the United States and Iran, energy supply disruptions and resulting price spikes are more likely.

item.title: Transnistria: A Conflict Unfrozen but Not Thawed
item.description: For the first time in three decades, there is clear and significant momentum toward Transnistrian reintegration, but converting this moment into a permanent solution requires vision, substantial financial resources, and delicate diplomacy.
